analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It adds one paragraph at head lines 757-765 of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md, under `inference_response_chunk`. The paragraph describes how streamed `auto` tool calls are fragmented across SSE chunks. The first chunk carries id, type, function.name and an empty function.arguments. Later chunks carry only `index` and a `function.arguments` fragment, and consumers concatenate fragments by `index`. It also cites libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMServer/Runtime/MLXOpenAIService.swift (`streamChatCompletionFrames`) as the source.

No code, wire schema, encryption path, authorization, attestation or key-handling change is present. The description is of the OpenAI-style chunk content that is already carried inside the encrypted `encrypted_data` payload (A-001 on the TB-002 leg). It does not alter the T-008 fail-closed encryption contract. Plaintext `data` remains described as empty when E2E encryption is active, and the new text does not reintroduce plaintext.

The doc is consumer-facing about chunk structure and grants no trust. Providers and consumers are treated as adversarial, and consumers must already handle malformed or adversarial provider tool-call fragments. The documentation does not claim validation guarantees. I found no new attack surface, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated or needs updating. The remaining units (the base text of the surrounding file) are unchanged context: the prefix-cache, capacity and autopilot descriptions, and T-041. They were examined and show no change. The cited Swift source and the `../architecture/inference.md#streamed-auto-tool-calls` anchor are outside the supplied evidence, so the behavior described there is unverified.
